title: How to Deep Clean a Kitchen? Kitchen Deep Cleaning Checklist
description: Follow this step-by-step kitchen deep cleaning checklist and learn how to deep clean your kitchen like a pro or book expert today.
content:
A quick wipe-down keeps your kitchen looking neat. But a proper kitchen deep cleaning transforms it.

If you have been wondering how to deep clean the kitchen properly, this step-by-step guide walks you through the entire process. From cabinets and appliances to hidden grease spots and bacteria hotspots, this complete kitchen deep cleaning checklist ensures nothing gets missed.

Let us get started.

Step 1: Prep And Declutter

Before we begin any kitchen deep cleaning, we know we need a clear workspace. We turn on some music, grab a microfiber cloth, degreaser, and a trash bag, and start clearing the countertops.

First, start with removing anything that does not belong in the kitchen. Mail, keys, random packaging. Gone. We also suggest emptying the sink and loading the dishwasher, so we have space to scrub and rinse properly.

Instantly, the kitchen feels more manageable.

Prep Checklist

  • Gather deep cleaning supplies (microfiber cloths, degreaser, all-purpose cleaner, scrub brushes)

  • Clear countertops completely

  • Remove items that belong in other rooms

  • Empty the sink

  • Load or empty the dishwasher

Preparation makes the rest of the deep cleaning process smoother and more efficient.

Step 2: Cabinets, Drawers & Pantry Deep Cleaning

The golden rule is to always work from top to bottom. Try to look up and start with the upper cabinets.

You should empty every cabinet and drawer completely. Yes, everything comes out. This is the only way to properly deep-clean kitchen storage areas.

Expired spices. Old packets. Broken utensils. They go straight into the trash.

Then you should wipe down cabinet interiors, shelves, and drawer corners. Grease tends to settle on cabinet doors and handles, so I use a degreaser to remove the sticky buildup.

Finally, reorganize everything neatly into zones.

Cabinets & Pantry Checklist

  • Empty all cabinets and drawers

  • Discard expired food and unused items

  • Wipe interior shelves and drawer bases

  • Degrease cabinet fronts and handles

  • Clean the tops of cabinets

  • Replace shelf liners if needed

  • Reorganize items neatly

Cabinet deep cleaning removes hidden grease and dust that routine cleaning often overlooks.

Step 3: Deep Cleaning Major Kitchen Appliances

Now comes the heavy-duty part of the kitchen deep cleaning checklist.

Refrigerator Deep Cleaning

Remove all food items and take out shelves and drawers. We suggest cleaning each piece thoroughly and paying special attention to the rubber door gasket where mold can develop.

Oven & Stovetop Deep Cleaning

Burnt food and grease buildup require a strong degreaser. You should remove burner grates, soak them, and scrub the oven interior and glass door carefully.

Dishwasher Cleaning

Most people forget this step. Do not forget to remove and clean the bottom filter and run an empty cycle with vinegar to eliminate odor and buildup.

Exhaust Hood Cleaning

The range hood filter collects grease quickly. You should remove it, soak it in degreaser, and wipe down the hood exterior.

Major Appliances Checklist

  • Empty and clean refrigerator shelves and drawers

  • Clean fridge door seals

  • Soak and scrub stovetop grates

  • Degrease the oven interior and door

  • Clean the dishwasher filter and run vinegar cycle

  • Remove and clean range hood filters

Deep cleaning appliances significantly improves hygiene and kitchen freshness.

Step 4: Small Appliances & Hidden Bacteria Hotspots

People used to skip these small details. Not anymore.

Coffee makers, air fryers, and toasters collect residue and moisture, which can become breeding grounds for bacteria.

You should descale your coffee machine using a vinegar solution. Unplug the toaster, empty the crumb tray, and wipe the exterior. I scrub the air fryer basket and heating coil area carefully.

The microwave also needs attention. Heating a bowl of water and vinegar for 5 minutes loosens grime, making it easy to wipe clean.

Small Appliances Checklist

  • Descale the coffee maker

  • Empty toaster crumb tray

  • Clean the air fryer basket and interior

  • Sanitize can opener blades

  • Disinfect knife block slots

  • Steam-clean microwave interior

These overlooked steps are what make a kitchen truly spotless.

Step 5: Sink, Countertops & Backsplash Scrubbing

With everything cleared off, spray the countertops and backsplash with an all-purpose cleaner.

Grease splashes behind the stove and near prep areas are common, then scrub gently but thoroughly.

Then focus on the sink.

Use baking soda to scrub the basin, clean the overflow hole, and soak the faucet aerator in vinegar to remove limescale. Running the garbage disposal with ice cubes and lemon peels leaves the entire kitchen smelling fresh.

Surfaces & Sink Checklist

  • Wipe down countertops

  • Clean backsplash tiles

  • Scrub sink basin

  • Clean faucet aerator

  • Sanitize sponge holders

  • Refresh garbage disposal

This stage instantly makes the kitchen look brighter and cleaner.

Step 6: Floors & Final Touches

The final step in any kitchen deep cleaning checklist is the floor.

Dust and crumbs fall during cleaning, so sweep thoroughly, making sure to reach under cabinets and appliances.

Then mop with a suitable floor cleaner, working your way toward the exit so you do not step on freshly cleaned floors.

Finally, you wipe light switches, outlet covers, and baseboards. Also, wash and sanitize trash bins as well.

Floors & Final Touches Checklist

  • Sweep or vacuum floors

  • Reach under appliances

  • Mop floors thoroughly

  • Clean baseboards

  • Sanitize trash and recycling bins

  • Wipe light switches and outlet covers

Walking back into a fully deep cleaned kitchen feels incredibly satisfying.
